subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
passage:
In the library period, a video of Siddharth tripping on the stage steps was going round the class. Comments piled up under it. Rehana held her phone under the desk. Ayaan had written “Gold medal for falling,” and others added laughing lines. She typed, “Nice landing champ,” and pressed send. Thirty likes in a minute. It felt like tossing a coin into a fountain; nobody could really be hurt. Zoya, beside her, put her phone away and said nothing.

Next morning Siddharth sat at the back with his hood up. The comments were all still there, fifty of them. Rehana read her own line as if Siddharth were reading it, and her stomach dropped. She deleted it and went to sit beside him.

qa.q: What did Rehana type under the video?
Why did the comment feel harmless to Rehana at first?
qa.a: Many others were doing the same, so it felt like tossing a coin into a fountain, and nobody seemed really hurt.

qa.q: What choice did Rehana make the next morning?
qa.a: Rehana deleted the comment and went to sit beside Siddharth.

qa.q: What might Siddharth have felt, sitting at the back with the hood up while the comments stayed?
qa.a: Siddharth probably felt exposed and ashamed, knowing every one of the fifty comments could be read.

grounding: A teenager adds a mocking comment to a viral video because many others are doing so, then realises the target sees every word.

passage:
Dear Himani,

I'm writing because I'm too ashamed to say this in class. On Tuesday the video of you slipping at the sports meet was all over our class group. Everyone was posting jokes, even Ritu and Deepak. Only Kabir said, “Stop it,” and we ignored him. I wrote one too: “Ground record for the fastest slide.” I told myself it was just a joke and would get lost among so many.

Then on Wednesday I saw you at the gate, checking your phone with your face closed, and I realised you had read every single one.

I deleted mine. This morning I told Mr. Rao what I did. He sat the whole group down at lunch and had the video taken down. I'm sorry, Himani.

Yash

qa.q: What joke did Yash write under the video?
qa.a: Yash wrote, “Ground record for the fastest slide.”

qa.q: Why did Yash think Himani would never see the joke?
qa.a: Yash assumed it was just a joke that would get lost among so many comments.

qa.q: What did Yash do after realising Himani had read every comment?
qa.a: Yash deleted the joke and told Mr. Rao what had been done.

qa.q: What might Himani have felt at the gate, checking a phone with a closed face?
qa.a: Himani probably felt exposed and hurt, reading each comment alone.

grounding: A teenager who added a mocking comment to a viral video writes to the target after seeing that every word was read.
